A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same tensorial message-passing framework and PointNet++ adaptation, despite the changed title. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original ModelNet40 normal-regression and classification experiments, frame/message ablations, data-efficiency curves and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 reports original experiments on ModelNet40, ShapeNet and ScanObjectNN, including frame-refinement, noise-robustness and PCA-frame comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 keeps predicted local frames fixed during message passing. V3 adds iterative frame refinement: an MLP predicts an SO(3) rotation after each layer, updates the local frame and transforms features into that updated frame (Section 4.3.1, Equations 14–15). This substantially extends the retained tensorial-message procedure.

E1.justification: V2 evaluates only ModelNet40 normal regression and classification. V3 retains both and adds ShapeNet part segmentation, real-world ScanObjectNN classification and evaluations under Gaussian input noise, substantially broadening tasks and input conditions.

E2.justification: Normal-regression comparisons expand from Luo et al. alone to include RS-CNN, DGCNN and GC-Conv (Table 1). ModelNet40 classification expands from CRIN alone to numerous comparators, including PointNet, TFN and both Vector Neurons variants (v3 Table 4). These are actual comparison rows using published scores; the PDFs do not establish that those baselines were rerun.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: the regression learning rate falls from 5e-3 to 2.5e-3, encoder sampling fractions change, and classification feature configurations and frame-prediction MLP sizes change. Figure 4 replaces classification-error scaling with normal-regression cosine-error scaling. V3 also introduces noise/jitter protocols and a 500-epoch ScanObjectNN setting.

E4.justification: V3 retains the learned/random-frame and scalar/tensor-message ablation, adds comparisons with and without iterative refinement, and tests PCA frames against learned frames. Appendix D and Figure 5 add noise-sensitivity analyses of predictions, complete frames and individual frame axes, including training with versus without jitter. The data-efficiency analysis also changes task.

E5.justification: V3 extends uncertainty depiction to robustness results through shaded bands in Figure 5, but does not explain their statistical meaning or sampling basis. Runtime reporting remains mean plus standard deviation over ten test-set loops in both versions. No increase in repeated training runs or newly specified seed counts is established.

E6.justification: Under revised settings, unrefined learned-frame tensor results change from 0.86 to 0.87 cosine similarity and from 88.3% to 88.0% ModelNet40 classification accuracy. V3 adds refined-model results, including 0.88 cosine similarity, 80.2 ShapeNet IoU and 81.0% ScanObjectNN accuracy, plus PCA and noise findings. Runtime values and Figure 4 results also change. These are not controlled performance gains across versions.

T1.justification: The central representation framework and invariance derivations remain. V3 adds a short proof of equivariance for local-frame construction in Appendix B and mathematical justification for refinement and feature transport in Equations 14–15. Equation 13 also corrects the missing inverse in v2's derivation.

C1.justification: The claims about general architectural applicability, tensorial communication and normal-regression performance remain. V3 adds iterative local-frame refinement as an explicit main contribution and claims that it strictly generalizes static local canonicalization, materially extending the paper's claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations for why refinement benefits from an expanding receptive field, why normal estimation is noise-sensitive, and why Gram–Schmidt makes later frame axes less robust. It newly acknowledges discontinuities and symmetric degeneracies in canonical frames and interprets PCA-versus-learned frame performance as task-dependent. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V3 documents refinement MLP dimensions, ShapeNet inputs and a full segmentation architecture and hyperparameter configuration. It revises existing architecture specifications and hardware/training-time reports, and newly discloses random-direction handling of parallel frame vectors. These additions materially expand implementation information beyond v2's two-task setup.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around canonicalization, adding frame averaging, learned canonicalization, approximate frame transitions and gauge-equivariant approaches, including Puny, Kaba, Du and Cohen. The earlier survey of handcrafted local-frame construction is removed. V3 also connects its data-efficiency discussion to newer work on broken symmetries and equivariant scaling.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations around local canonicalization. ModelNet40 classification moves into Appendix D, while experimental details become a separate Appendix E. The revised narrative emphasizes communication between frames and their iterative refinement.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the scalar-message illustration as an early scalar-versus-tensor comparison, adds refinement to the pipeline diagram and redraws the frame-transformation illustration. It replaces Figure 4's plotted task, adds the six-panel robustness Figure 5, expands comparison tables and relocates classification results. These are substantial display changes beyond the conference-template update.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens scrutiny of the central mechanism: refinement ablations, PCA alternatives and noise tests address frame-estimation questions left largely untested in v2, while segmentation, real-world classification and broader comparator tables address its narrow empirical validation. Added mathematical justification, explicit degeneracy caveats and clearer diagrams improve assessability. Accuracy results still lack repeated-run uncertainty, and Figure 5's bands are undefined, but these remaining weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and explanation.
